title: Why the C-melody saxophone faded
summary: The C-melody lacked printed parts, since orchestrations were written for alto and tenor.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Speaking of Trumbauer. You spoke about the C-melody earlier when you talked about its functions, its use when you first took it up. Why do you think it just suddenly phased out? The tenor seemed to take over and in the alto.
They were the ones it was written for. All your orchestrations --
Why didn't anyone write for the C-melody anymore?

Well, I don't know. Not everybody was a soloist. You came up and you played either first, second alto in the band. The parts were there for you. If you played print orchestrations, you -- there were first and second alto parts, and the parts were written that way, otherwise you would have to take -- I used to play them on the C-melody.
